CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit to evaluate the effectiveness of the adjusted treatment plan for generalized anxiety disorder, insomnia, persistent fatigue, and tension-type headaches, with a particular focus on the newly introduced amitriptyline and its impact on fatigue and sleep quality.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. John Smith presents for his follow-up appointment, bringing with him an updated symptom diary that reflects both the benefits and challenges encountered since the last visit. He reports that his generalized anxiety disorder remains stable, with the sertraline 300 mg daily regimen effectively managing his baseline anxiety levels. However, he continues to experience sporadic anxiety spikes, especially during high-pressure work situations, requiring the use of lorazepam 1 mg approximately twice weekly.
Regarding insomnia, Mr. Smith expresses satisfaction with the recent addition of amitriptyline 10 mg at bedtime, noting a significant improvement in sleep continuity. He now averages about 7 hours of sleep per night, with fewer nocturnal awakenings, attributing this positive change to the combined effects of trazodone and amitriptyline. Nonetheless, he still occasionally wakes due to anxiety, particularly when under stress.
The frequency of tension-type headaches has shown slight improvement, now occurring approximately once every ten days, with an intensity rating of 3 out of 10. Mr. Smith has successfully managed these headaches with ibuprofen 600 mg as needed, although he remains open to exploring additional non-pharmacological interventions, such as physical therapy or mindfulness practices, to further alleviate headache frequency.
In terms of persistent fatigue, Mr. Smith reports a modest reduction in cognitive fog and an overall improvement in energy levels since starting amitriptyline. He describes feeling more alert during the day, particularly in the afternoons, but still experiences some fatigue that he finds challenging to shake off completely. He continues to implement short breaks at work, which he believes are beneficial.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder - diagnosed in 2021 2. Insomnia - diagnosed in 2021 3. Tension-Type Headaches - diagnosed in 2021 4. Hypertension - diagnosed in 2020, currently well-controlled on lisinopril 10 mg daily
MEDICATIONS
1. Sertraline 300 mg daily (continued) 2. Trazodone 100 mg at bedtime (continued) 3. Lisinopril 10 mg daily (continued) 4. Ibuprofen 600 mg as needed for headache relief (continued) 5.
